appraisal_events.evidence: « Non, car il a l’air d’un tapir… cela se perd dans des joues encaustiquées qui lui donnent un air assez mameluck. On sent que le frotteur doit passer tous les matins. » … « Du reste, comme il n’est pas reçu, ce snobisme n’aurait pas à s’exercer. »
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme de Guermantes turns the Iéna household into salon amusement — grotesque physical caricature of the son, then a mock-indulgent defense that ends in the flat verdict that the family is not received; the narrator ironizes her delivery ('comme s’il y eût eu à son avis incompatibilité absolue entre le snobisme et l’intelligence') without softening the exclusion it pronounces.

appraisal_events.evidence: « reprit-elle sans songer qu’elle n’encourageait pas beaucoup de la sorte la princesse de Parme » ; « Je me demande ce que dira le prince de Guermantes, qui l’appelle Mme Iéna, s’il apprend que je suis allée chez elle. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator marks the princesse de Parme as the unregarded casualty of the duchesse's wit: urged toward the Iénas and then told they are unreceivable, she is left anxiously anticipating the prince de Guermantes's contempt for a visit she has already made.

status_effects.explanation: The household is placed outside valued social space by explicit verdict ('il n’est pas reçu') and by the prince's title-stripping nickname 'Mme Iéna'.

She holds the floor and dispenses verdicts that both the princesse de Parme and M. de Bréauté solicit; the narrator's irony about her mannered performance qualifies but does not cancel her local command of the exchange.
She ends the exchange exposed and apprehensive, dependent on how a social superior will judge a visit the duchesse encouraged and then discredited.

ambiguities: The body of the mockery targets the unnamed 'jeune duc' (the Iéna son), who is descriptor-identified and not on the reference sheet; the only named surface form for that household in the passage is 'Mme Iéna', the prince de Guermantes's title-stripping truncation, which denotes the mother. The snub is therefore recorded against 'Mme Iéna' as the passage's named stand-in for the excluded family.

The narration is double-edged toward Mme de Guermantes: her wit is socially dominant, yet the narrator flags her equation of intelligence with non-snobbery and her heedlessness of the princesse de Parme. The reading committed to here keeps her rhetorical gain but only at +1, since the same sentences that display her mastery also expose its thoughtlessness.
